chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ribi'i ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever frees a Muslim, Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, will free one limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for freeing a Muslim slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on manumission, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) underscores the profound spiritual efficacy of freeing a Muslim slave, promising that Allah will liberate each of the emancipator's limbs from the Hellfire in exchange for each limb of the freed slave. This specific bodily correspondence highlights the tangible, physical nature of the reward in Shia jurisprudence and theology. It serves as a key textual basis for the virtue of *al-'itq* as a means of expiation and spiritual purification.
